messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER: High error rate detected for cross-region routing (eu-west2 -> us-west1). Alert ID CRR-20260315-01. metric: routing_policy_misroute.v2 > 10% over 3m.

maria: ack — i'm on it. paging oncall.

dylan: seeing a large spike in 5xxs from the gateway when routing eu-west2 -> us-west1. traces show elevated latency and a few 523/524s.

alex: adding context — DNS TTLs for regional pinning are shorter than we expect for some hosts, looks like pins expired earlier than our controller predicted. pulling cache counts now.

maria: running query to confirm: `SELECT count(*) FROM requests WHERE target_region='us-west1' AND latency>2000 GROUP BY source_region;` — surge primarily from eu-west2.

ops_lead: quick question — any confirmed customer-facing 503/504 reports?
support-bot: support alerted — two customer alerts: acct-835 and acct-1201 showing increased errors to EU endpoints. ticketed.

maria: starting mitigation: temporary routing override to prefer local region for eu-west2 while we investigate.

maria: applying override with API call:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.internal/routing/override \
  -d '{"region":"eu-west2","preferred":"eu-west2","reason":"temp-mitigation: cross-region misroute"}' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ROUTE_TOKEN"
```

maria: override applied, waiting ~30s for propagation across proxies.

dylan: telemetry — cross-region egress from eu-west2 -> us-west1 dropped quickly. error rate down to ~6% after 45s.

alex: i'm still seeing a subset of stale DNS caches honoring old pins (short TTL churn). i'm triggering a pin-refresh on the controller: 
```
kubectl -n routing exec -it rollup-controller -- curl -X POST /v1/pins/refresh -d '{"region":"eu-west2"}'
```

maria: note — some clients retried during the spike and saw failures, so expect a short-lived customer-facing spike ~2-3 minutes. support has been notified to correlate.

support-bot: created incident ticket INC-20260315-CRR and connected to statuspage. draft outbound message queued.

ops_lead: good. we need the root cause before we roll everything back. dylan you on logs, alex you coordinate with DNS/controller team?
dylan: digging into deploy history — there's a config diff at 03:12 UTC that adjusted latency-steering weights; it lowered the local weighting for eu-west2 in a canary patch. author is @eng-runtime-ci. this would explain increased cross-region routing.
alex: confirmed. combined with the shorter TTLs, the lowered local weight allowed clients to drift to us-west1. also found a race in the routing proxy where pins that should be refreshed are occasionally accepted after TTL expiration (pin refresh race).

maria: applying quick patch: revert the canary weight change and enable a strict pin enforcement flag to prevent accepting expired pins during refresh.

maria: commands run: `revert /changes/steering-weight-0312` and `set routing.pin_strict_mode=true` — pushing canary now.

dylan: metrics trending back to normal. error rate down to baseline (~0.7%) and latency normalized after the revert.

maria: preparing handoff — i've hit my oncall window (55m). Handoff summary: root cause likely steering-weight canary + DNS TTL churn + pin-refresh race. Mitigations performed: routing override, revert weight change, enable pin_strict_mode. Customer impact: transient 5xx spike affecting a small subset (acct-835, acct-1201) for ~3-6 minutes. Next actions: full RCA and postmortem; add tests/guards to prevent simultaneous steering-weight changes during pin refreshes.

sam: acknowledged — taking over. i will monitor for 2 hours and coordinate the postmortem with eng-runtime and routing teams. tagging @eng-runtime @eng-releases.

maria: logs, queries and commands above are attached to the ticket. good handoff. :white_check_mark: 

statuspage-bot: Statuspage draft: "Partial degraded performance for EU region — mitigated. Investigating root cause." PR queued for review.
sam: quick request — please update statuspage with a timeline and affected hostnames when available.

alex: note for postmortem — we'll add a regression test for TTL + weight-change interactions and implement a rollout guard that blocks steering weight changes when pin-heavy operations are in-flight.
dylan: filing follow-up GH issue GH-4821: "prevent steering weight canary from lowering local region weight without explicit pin-safe flag".

maria: thanks all. attaching perf graphs and correlation logs to INC-20260315-CRR now, handing off to sam. :coffee:
